Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects CKB Escrow: decentralized escrow for goods and services on Nervos CKB OPEN **Project Summary:** CKB Escrow is a standalone decentralized escrow app for goods and services between known parties on Nervos CKB. A buyer can create and fund an escrow for a known seller, the seller can mark the work or goods as delivered, the buyer can release funds or open a dispute, and an arbitrator can resolve disputed escrows to either party. The project is not a marketplace or storefront; it focuses on the escrow workflow itself, with wallet-first identity, role-aware actions, indexer-backed escrow history, and a product UI supported by a separate protocol/studio interface. **Tools used:** - Rust for CKB script development - CKB RISC-V VM contract model - `ckb-std` - `ckb-testtool` - Docker reproducible contract builds - `@offckb/cli` for deployment tooling - CCC / CKB wallet integration - TypeScript - Next.js - React - Tailwind CSS - shadcn-style UI primitives - Postgres-ready escrow indexer storage - Neon/Postgres planned for hosted production history - Vercel planned for frontend hosting **Current features:** - Buyer-first escrow product UI - Wallet-first identity, no email/password registration - Testnet/mainnet network selection in the frontend - Buyer can create and fund escrow for a known seller - Seller can discover escrows they belong to and mark delivered - Buyer can release funds, cancel where allowed, dispute, or refund after deadline - Arbitrator can review disputed escrows and resolve to buyer or seller - Role-aware escrow discovery for buyer, seller, and arbitrator - Active and past escrow views - Terminal escrow history through indexer-backed recovery design - Escrow detail “deal room” with timeline, status, parties, actions, and receipt mode - Dispute evidence flow using off-chain evidence metadata and hashes - `/studio` route for protocol/debug/deployment workflows - Contract documentation, frontend documentation, and deployment notes - Reproducible build/checksum workflow for the contract - OffCKB deployment tooling support **Planned features:** - Complete full hosted testnet end-to-end validation: - buyer creates and funds escrow - seller marks delivered - buyer releases funds - buyer cancels before delivery - buyer refunds after deadline - buyer/seller opens dispute - arbitrator resolves to buyer or seller - Improve the hosted indexer so escrow history syncs continuously instead of only through API-triggered

Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects Cellora: a multi-tenant indexing and query service for CKB OPEN **Project Summary:** Cellora is a managed indexing and query layer for CKB, designed as a production data backbone for DApps that would rather not run their own full node, indexer and database stack. It normalizes blocks, transactions and cells into a PostgreSQL store with indexes tuned for the dominant access patterns (by lock hash, type hash, outpoint), exposes REST and GraphQL surfaces behind API-key auth and per-key rate limiting, and treats reorgs as a first-class case rather than an edge case. **Tools used:** Rust (Axum, async-graphql, SQLx), PostgreSQL, Redis, `ckb-jsonrpc-types`, `reqwest`, Docker / Kubernetes, OpenTelemetry + Prometheus. **Current features:** - Block polling loop against a CKB JSON-RPC endpoint (`get_tip_block_number`, `get_block_by_number`, `get_blockchain_info`) - Parser and writer that normalize blocks → transactions → cells - Live/dead cell accounting via `consumed_*` columns - One-transaction-per-block write path — the database never observes a partial block - Indexer-state tracking for tip recovery across restarts - Graceful shutdown on `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` **Planned features:** - REST API (blocks, cells, stats, health, cursor pagination) - GraphQL endpoint via `async-graphql` - API-key authentication (Argon2-hashed) with tiered rate limits backed by a Redis token bucket - Reorg detection and transactional rollback with an audit log - Range partitioning on the `cells` table by block number - Webhook delivery with HMAC signatures and retry queue - GraphQL subscriptions for live cell updates - Grafana dashboards and OpenTelemetry tracing - Dashboard for API-key management, usage charts, and a query explorer **Deployed on:** Dev chain today. Testnet is the next milestone, mainnet after reorg handling lands. **Link to repository:** https://github.com/Antismart/cellora **Link to hosted version of project:** Not yet hosted publicly — happy to stand up a testnet-backed preview for reviewers who want to kick the tires. **Screenshots:** Not applicable at this stage — Cellora is backend infrastructure with no UI yet. Architecture overview with diagrams is at [`docs/architecture-overview.md`](https://github.com/Antismart/cellora/blob/main/docs/architecture-overview.md) in the repo. **Request for feedback:** I'd value both design-review input and product-market input from this community. *On the design (review):* - The data model
